html:
The Wiilman are an Aboriginal people of the inland southwest of Western Australia, in the open woodland of what is now the Wheatbelt and Great Southern, around Wagin and Narrogin. They are one of the language groups of the Noongar.

Their neighbours were the Ballardong to the north, the Pinjarup and Kaniyang to the west and the Goreng to the south. Noongar life followed six seasons, moving between the coast, rivers and inland country as foods ripened.

After the Swan River Colony was founded in 1829, settlers took up grazing land in the southwest. In the early 1900s the clearing of the Wheatbelt for wheat farms changed Wiilman country almost completely. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
